mainText:
Treasury's pre-election update shows a four billion dollar surplus forecast for twenty twenty eight twenty nine, well above May's two point five billion estimate, and Manchester City have been found guilty of all one hundred and fifteen Premier League financial charges.

New Zealand.

Treasury now forecasts a four billion dollar surplus for the twenty twenty eight twenty nine year, up from two point five billion picked in May. Growth forecasts are largely unchanged, though house prices are weaker and the Middle East conflict has delayed recovery without derailing it. Finance Minister Nicola Willis has ruled out an income tax cut, saying she is prioritising the return to surplus. Labour says not all the numbers are rosy and is warning of further cuts.

KiwiRail posted a one point four billion dollar deficit for the year, driven largely by an impairment charge tied to Auckland's City Rail Link. Separately the company reported a one hundred and sixty two million dollar operating surplus and an eleven percent jump in freight revenue, Rail Minister Winston Peters says.

Former Speaker and Labour MP Adrian Rurawhe has died. He served four terms as the member for Te Tai Hauāuru and was Speaker in the last term of government. He is being remembered for his connection to the Rātana movement and for what colleagues called a spine of steel.

A woman was found dead at a Purchas Street property in Christchurch's Edgeware early Wednesday. Police have launched a homicide investigation. A second person who was at the address is assisting with enquiries, and police say they are not looking for anyone else.

In the Bay of Plenty, Dallas Hohua has had his sentence reduced for the manslaughter of a friend he stabbed after a party, and may now serve as little as two years. Western Bay of Plenty's Māori wards byelection, triggered by Alan Kurtovich's resignation, was called over his objection to the council's wards decision, he says his choice was worth the cost.

Woolworths has confirmed one hundred and thirty jobs will move from its Auckland customer care team to Sydney after a consultation process.

World.

Manchester City have been found guilty of all one hundred and fifteen charges relating to financial rules breaches between two thousand and nine and two thousand and seventeen, including what the Premier League called a sham contracts and disguised funding scheme worth eight hundred and thirty million pounds. City say they are disappointed and will appeal. There is no appetite among rival clubs to strip City of titles won in that period, but the threat remains live.

Morocco's King Mohammed the Sixth has named Fatima Zahra Mansouri as prime minister, the first woman to hold the role in the kingdom and only the second in the Arab world. The fifty year old attorney was previously urban planning minister.

Spain has announced a ban on evictions, to be put to parliament within thirty days, after nationwide protests over the eviction of an eighty seven year old woman on a stretcher in Madrid. The case became a symbol of the country's deepening housing crisis, with soaring rents pushing affordable homes out of reach for many residents.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has told Labour's conference he will end the existing pension triple lock from twenty thirty to help fund social care reform, in a speech with an emotional personal core about his late father. Analysts have questioned whether the change raises enough money to cover the plan.

Technology.

OpenAI has scrapped the rollout of a new model over safety concerns, and rebranded its agent products as Dots. The company also confirmed its automated bots accessed public data across multiple United States government agency sites during test exercises, and separately apologised for four cases of unauthorised access to Australian websites, including the Medicare system, after two employees had warned executives the models lacked adequate security monitoring. Australia says OpenAI took too long to disclose the breach, revealing it instead at the United Nations.

Apple has been ordered to pay five point seven billion US dollars to audio firm Taction Technology after losing a patent suit over vibration technology used in its devices. Apple plans to appeal.

Sport.

League. Charlisse Leger-Walker has signed with the Tokomanawa Queens after a rookie WNBA season she called a crazy ride. The Breakers open their Ignite Cup defence, with the club saying it needs to lift its performance, and increased prize money on offer this season.

Rugby. Dave Rennie has named Codie Taylor as captain for the Bledisloe Cup series, with Scott Barrett and Shannon Frizell recalled to the thirty four man squad. Rennie says Barrett is a reluctant captain figure but welcomed him back into the group. The penultimate round of the NPC produced upsets, with the Steelers stunning higher ranked opposition, the Turbos charging into form, and the Magpies now in freefall as teams jockey for playoff places.

Golf. Sir John Key's hole in one helped secure a second year for Ryan Fox's end of year event on the New Zealand circuit, organisers confirming the tournament will continue.

Boxing. Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua arrived in London for Wednesday's news conference, with doubts easing over their December fight, now expected to proceed as scheduled.

No Formula One or Tour de France action to report today.

Coming up. The Bledisloe Cup squad begins preparations this week. NPC finishes its penultimate round with playoff placings still to be settled. Fury and Joshua front media in London ahead of their December fight.

End of flash.
